Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

believe verb

also believe me, why should I take your word for it?, take someone’s word for it

classical

Phaedr. 3.10.1: perīculōsum est crēdere et nōn crēdere
Traupman 278

crēdō, crēdere, crēdidī, crēditum

verb, third conjugation · Conjugation on Wiktionary

believe (a person, a story); believe that, think

The person or the story believed in the dative (mihi crēde, believe me); what one believes in an accusative and infinitive (tē crēdō surripuisse, I believe you stole it, Phaedr. 1.10.10). Said in passing, crēdō is “I suppose”.

Other words

  • opīnor, opīnārī, opīnātus sum — believe, suppose; opīnor in passing, “I believe”

    verb, first conjugation, deponent · also used · classical · Cic. Tusc. 1.92: nōndum, opīnor, est experrēctus; Traupman 109: Sīc opīnor. · Conjugation on Wiktionary

Examples

  • perīculōsum est crēdere et nōn crēdere

    it is dangerous both to believe and not to believePhaedr. 3.10.1

  • crēde mihi, quicquid discis, tibi discis

    believe me, whatever you learn, you learn for yourselfPetr. 46.1

  • at memoria minuitur. crēdō, nisi eam exerceās

    “But memory fades.” I suppose it does, unless you exercise it.Cic. Sen. 21

  • hanc enim pater sē vīdisse affirmat, puer nōn crēdit

    for Dad says he saw the fox; the boy doesn’t believe itLibellus VII, Diēs ūnus Osoitsae

  • Cūr tibi crēdam?

    Why should I take your word for it?Traupman 111

  • Mihi crēde.

    Believe me.Traupman 130, 134; Cic. Cat. 1.6 (Lewis & Short s.v. crēdō)

See also believe in, seem, I think so, true, think.
